mainTopic: Which offspring and substitutes of קדשים are offered: שלמים, תודה and עולה
overview: רבי חייא brings a ברייתא that reads two limits out of 'אם כשב הוא מקריב'. The first limit is that a שלמים's offspring is offered but the offspring's offspring is not. The second is that only a שלמים's offspring is offered, not that of other קדשים. The גמרא searches for what the second limit excludes and settles on the offspring of מעשר בהמה, because we cannot learn the possible from the impossible (בכור). Next, רבי פפייס's testimony about a cow eaten on פסח whose offspring was eaten 'on the חג' raises a בל תאחר problem. רב זביד answers that the animal was sick on שבועות, while רב אשי reads 'חג' as שבועות. The testimony itself shows, against רבי אליעזר, that a שלמים's offspring is offered. A new משנה rules that the offspring and substitutes of a תודה are like a תודה but come without loaves, and a ברייתא gives the source. A further משנה treats the substitute of an עולה and its offspring as an עולה. It also brings a dispute about the male calf of a female set aside as an עולה. רבה בר בר חנה and רבא explain why only the second case is disputed. Then רב חסדא and רבא resolve a contradiction in רבי אלעזר's view, and רבא's answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רבי יהושע בן לוי: the second-generation offspring is not offered
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא teaches that the word 'כשב' shows that the first offspring of a שלמים is offered, but the offspring of that offspring is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא taught a ברייתא to support רבי יהושע בן לוי. The פסוק says 'If he sacrifices a lamb.' From this we learn that the first offspring is offered, but the second offspring is not offered.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא from רבי חייא as support for רבי יהושע בן לוי's view that the offspring of the offspring of a שלמים is never offered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא reads the word 'כשב' (lamb) as a limiting word. It allows one generation, the direct offspring of the שלמים, but not a second generation. This backs up רבי יהושע בן לוי's claim that even those who allow the offspring to be offered agree that the grand-offspring is not.

keyTerms.meaning: to support (someone's opinion)
the first offspring: the direct young of the קרבן
the second offspring: the young of the young
is offered on the מזבח

phrases.aramaic: תָּנֵי רַבִּי חִיָּיא לְסַיּוֹעֵי לְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Chiyya teaches [a baraita] to support Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi:
"If he sacrifices a lamb"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 3:7

phrases.english: — the first offspring is offered,
the second offspring is not offered.
phrases.notes: The 'second offspring' is the young born to the offspring of the שלמים.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנֵי רַבִּי חִיָּיא לְסַיּוֹעֵי לְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings ברייתא support for רבי יהושע בן לוי's statement made just before this point in the daf.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יהושע בן לוי's view that everyone agrees the offspring of the offspring of a שלמים is not offered
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא taught by רבי חייא that reads the word 'כשב' in ויקרא 3:7 as a limitation

steps.title: The word 'הוא' limits offering to the offspring of a שלמים only
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: the word 'הוא' teaches that the offspring of a שלמים is offered, but not the offspring of any other קדשים.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'He' (it) is offered, but the offspring of all other sacrifices is not offered.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives a second limit from the same פסוק. Only a שלמים's offspring is offered, not the offspring of other kinds of קרבנות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'הוא' looks extra, so it is read as pointing to the offspring of the שלמים. That gives an exclusion: offspring of other קדשים are not offered. This new limit is what the גמרא will question next.

keyTerms.meaning: 'it/he': an extra word in the פסוק, read here as a limitation
all other sanctified animals (קרבנות)

phrases.english: "He" (it) — is offered,
phrases.notes: The word הוא in the פסוק is read as pointing to the young of the שלמים.

phrases.english: but the offspring of all [other] sacrifices is not offered.

steps.triggerLanguage: הוּא — קָרֵב, וְאֵין וְלַד כׇּל הַקֳּדָשִׁים קָרֵב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with a second limitation drawn from the same פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only the offspring of a שלמים may be offered; offspring of other קדשים may not.

steps.title: Which other offering's young could the פסוק be excluding?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which offspring the פסוק excludes. עולה and אשם are males and have no young. The young of a חטאת is already known by הלכה to be left to die.
steps.simpleTranslation: Which offering's offspring is this talking about? If it means a burnt offering or guilt offering, those are males and cannot have young. If it means a sin offering, we already know by a הלכה passed down by tradition that its young is left to die.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the second limit. It seems there is no case left for the פסוק to teach.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The exclusion has to be about some specific kind of קרבן. Yet each option fails. עולה and אשם cannot give birth, and the חטאת case is already covered by a הלכה למשה מסיני. So the word 'הוא' seems to have nothing to exclude.

keyTerms.meaning: burnt offering (always a male animal)
guilt offering (always a male animal)
sin offering (can be a female)
they learned it as a הלכה by tradition
it goes to death: it is left to die

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the גמרא is saying the פסוק is wrong. It agrees that the offspring of these קרבנות are not offered. It is only asking why a פסוק is needed to teach it.

phrases.english: The offspring of what [offering]?
If of a burnt offering or a guilt offering —

phrases.aramaic: זְכָרִים הֵם, וְלָא בְּנֵי וָלָד הֵם.
phrases.english: they are males, and are not capable of having offspring.
If of a sin offering —
they learned it as a halacha [by tradition] that it goes to its death.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions what the second limit in the ברייתא (step 2) could be coming to teach.
steps.kashyaTarget: The derivation from 'הוא' that the offspring of other קדשים is not offered
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Every possible case is either impossible (male קרבנות) or already known from a הלכה (חטאת), so the פסוק seems unneeded.

steps.title: רבינא: the פסוק comes to exclude the offspring of a מעשר animal
steps.stepSummary: רבינא answers that the exclusion is about the offspring of an animal set aside as מעשר בהמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: the פסוק comes to include the offspring of a tithe animal.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא finds a case for the פסוק. A מעשר animal can be female and give birth, so the פסוק teaches that its young is not offered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מעשר בהמה is taken from the herd, males and females alike. So unlike עולה and אשם, it can have young. That gives the word 'הוא' a real case to exclude.

keyTerms.meaning: to include (a case in the rule)
the offspring of an animal set aside as מעשר בהמה

phrases.english: Ravina said: [It comes] to include the offspring of a tithe animal.
phrases.notes: 'Include' here means it falls under the same rule: that offspring is not offered either.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 3 by naming a case the פסוק is needed for.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies a new case the פסוק applies to
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק seemed to have no case to exclude.
steps.terutzMaskana: It excludes the offspring of a מעשר בהמה animal.

steps.title: No פסוק is needed for a מעשר animal's young: it comes from בכור by 'עברה'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבינא. The rule for a מעשר animal's offspring is already learned from בכור through the matching word 'עברה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do I need a פסוק for the offspring of a tithe animal? We already learn it from the firstborn through the matching words 'passing' and 'passing'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבינא's answer. The case he named is already covered by a גזירה שוה linking מעשר to בכור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both מעשר and בכור use a form of the word 'עברה' in the תורה, so they share laws. A בכור is always male and never has young to offer. Through this link, מעשר is treated the same way, so the פסוק 'הוא' again seems extra.

keyTerms.meaning: why do I need a פסוק? (the rule is already known)
the matching word 'passing' used for both מעשר and בכור: a גזירה שוה
a firstborn animal, which is always male
learns or derives (a law from another source)

steps.whyThisMatters: This puts the question of what 'הוא' comes to teach back on the table. The next step answers it.

phrases.english: [For] the offspring of a tithe animal, why do I need a verse?
"Passing" "passing"
phrases.notes: The two words come from ויקרא 27:32 ('יעבור', about מעשר) and שמות 13:12 ('והעברת', about a בכור).

phrases.english: it is derived from the firstborn!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבינא's answer in step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבינא's claim that the פסוק is needed for the offspring of a מעשר animal
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The rule is already known through a גזירה שוה ('עברה' 'עברה') from בכור, so the פסוק would still be extra.

steps.title: The verse is still needed: you cannot learn the possible from the impossible
steps.stepSummary: The word 'הוא' is still needed for the offspring of מעשר. Without it, we might say that בכור, which cannot give birth, cannot teach us about מעשר, which can.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was necessary. You might have thought: we do not learn something that is possible from something that is impossible. So the פסוק teaches us.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from Step 5. The פסוק is still needed even though we have the matching word 'עברה' from בכור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בכור is always a male, so it can never have an offspring. A מעשר animal can be female and can give birth. So we might have refused to learn the rule about a מעשר's offspring from בכור. That is why the פסוק 'הוא' is needed to teach it directly.

keyTerms.meaning: It was necessary
You might have thought to say
We do not learn a case where something is possible from a case where it is impossible
So it teaches us

steps.whatToRemember: The offspring of a מעשר animal is not offered on the מזבח. 'הוא' teaches this directly, because בכור alone could not teach it.

phrases.english: It was necessary,
phrases.notes: He means the word 'הוא' in the פסוק is still needed for מעשר.

phrases.english: it would have entered your mind to say:
we do not learn the possible from the impossible,
phrases.notes: A בכור is a male and can never give birth, but a מעשר animal can.

phrases.english: so it teaches us.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 5 that the verse is not needed.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that the verse is needed because the other source (the גזירה שוה from בכור) could be rejected
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We might have said a בכור, which cannot give birth, cannot teach about the offspring of מעשר
steps.terutzMaskana: The verse 'הוא' teaches directly that the offspring of מעשר is not offered

steps.title: Quoting the testimony of רבי יהושע and רבי פפייס
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's testimony about the offspring of a שלמים, to start a new discussion.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע and רבי פפייס testified, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is quoting a new line from the משנה. This sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי פפייס tells of a cow brought as a שלמים and eaten on פסח, and its offspring was eaten as a שלמים 'on the חג'. The גמרא will now ask about the time gap between the two festivals.

keyTerms.meaning: Testified, gave testimony about a ruling
And so on: the rest of the משנה is assumed

phrases.aramaic: הֵעִיד רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ וְרַבִּי פַּפְּיָיס כּוּ׳.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua and Rabbi Pappeyas testified, etc.
phrases.notes: The rest of the משנה: the cow was eaten on פסח, and its offspring was eaten 'on the חג'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה after the previous discussion ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The offspring of a שלמים is itself offered as a שלמים

steps.title: According to רבא, the offspring should have been eaten by שבועות
steps.stepSummary: רבא holds that after one festival passes, the owner breaks בל תאחר every day. So why did they wait from פסח until סוכות to eat the offspring?
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רבא, who said: once one festival has passed over sacred animals, each day the owner breaks 'do not delay'. He should have eaten it already from שבועות!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the story in the משנה using רבא's rule about delaying offerings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא understands 'חג' as סוכות. But after פסח, the next festival is שבועות. By רבא's rule, waiting past שבועות means breaking בל תאחר every day, so a proper story should not show waiting until סוכות.

keyTerms.meaning: The prohibition against delaying the bringing of a promised offering
A pilgrimage festival (פסח, שבועות, סוכות)
Another name for שבועות
Sacred animals set aside as offerings

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'חג' is first understood as סוכות, which is the usual meaning. Later רב אשי will read it differently.

phrases.english: And according to Rava, who said:

phrases.aramaic: קָדָשִׁים, כֵּיוָן שֶׁעָבַר עֲלֵיהֶם רֶגֶל אֶחָד,
phrases.english: sacred animals, once one festival has passed over them,
each and every day he transgresses regarding them
the prohibition 'do not delay',
phrases.notes: דברים 23:22

phrases.english: he should have eaten it already from Shavuot!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the story quoted in Step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי פפייס's story that the offspring was eaten on the חג (סוכות)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: By רבא's rule, waiting past שבועות breaks בל תאחר, so the story describes something forbidden

steps.title: The animal was sick on שבועות
steps.stepSummary: רב זביד, in the name of רבא, answers that the owner could not bring it on שבועות because it was sick.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב זביד said in the name of רבא: for example, where it was sick on שבועות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The owner did not delay on purpose; something stopped him on שבועות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A sick animal cannot be brought as an offering. So the delay until סוכות was forced, and the owner did not break בל תאחר.

keyTerms.meaning: For example, such as
Sick

phrases.english: Rav Zevid said in the name of Rava:
for example, where it was sick on Shavuot.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the case to a special situation where the owner was forced to delay
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The owner delayed on purpose until סוכות
steps.terutzMaskana: The animal was sick on שבועות, so the delay was not his fault

steps.title: 'חג' here means שבועות
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי gives a different answer: the 'חג' in the משנה is שבועות itself, so there was no delay.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: what is the 'חג' that is taught? It is the festival of שבועות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second answer to the same challenge. רב אשי rereads the word 'חג'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'חג' means שבועות, the offspring was eaten at the very next festival after פסח. Then no festival was skipped and there is no question of בל תאחר at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Festival; usually means סוכות
The festival of שבועות
That is taught (in the משנה)

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
What is the 'Festival' that is also taught?
The festival of Shavuot.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: מַאי ״חַג״ נָמֵי דְּקָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to the challenge in Step 8, different from רב זביד's answer in Step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereads a word in the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'חג' means סוכות, so the owner waited past שבועות
steps.terutzMaskana: 'חג' means שבועות, so there was no delay

steps.title: Why רב זביד does not read 'חג' as שבועות
steps.stepSummary: The other opinion, רב זביד, says that when the משנה mentions פסח and means שבועות, it says 'עצרת', not 'חג'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one? Wherever it teaches 'פסח', it teaches 'עצרת'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רב זביד did not give רב אשי's simple answer, and explains his reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב זביד looks at how the משנה usually speaks. When פסח is mentioned and שבועות is meant, the משנה uses the word 'עצרת'. Since this משנה says 'חג', it must mean סוכות, so רב זביד needs the answer about the sick animal.

keyTerms.meaning: And the other one (the other אמורא)
The festival of פסח

steps.whatToRemember: There are two answers for the testimony: רב זביד says 'חג' is סוכות and the animal was sick on שבועות; רב אשי says 'חג' is שבועות.

phrases.english: And the other one?
phrases.notes: This is רב זביד: why didn't he answer like רב אשי?

phrases.english: Wherever it teaches 'Pesach',
it teaches 'Atzeret'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why רב זביד in Step 9 rejects רב אשי's reading in Step 10.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רב אשי's reading of 'חג' as שבועות, from רב זביד's view
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה's normal style next to פסח is 'עצרת', not 'חג', for שבועות

steps.title: Then what was the testimony teaching?
steps.stepSummary: Based on the earlier answers, the גמרא asks what point רבי פפייס's testimony was making.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, what did his testimony come to teach?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks: if the delay is explained away (the animal was sick, or it was eaten on שבועות), then what new idea was רבי פפייס testifying about?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Simply read, the testimony seemed to show that waiting until סוכות is allowed. But steps 9-10 removed that idea, so the testimony no longer seems to teach anything about delay. The גמרא now needs a new purpose for it.

keyTerms.meaning: If so; if that is true
Testimony

phrases.english: If so,
phrases.notes: He means: if we accept the answers of רב זביד or רב אשי, that no real delay happened.

phrases.english: what is his testimony?
phrases.notes: In other words, what new thing did רבי פפייס come to tell us?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the answers in steps 9-11. Those answers removed the delay issue, so the testimony now seems to have no purpose.
steps.kashyaTarget: The purpose of רבי פפייס's testimony in the משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the testimony is not about delay, it appears to teach nothing new.

steps.title: The testimony rejects רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: The testimony teaches that the offspring of a שלמים may be brought as a שלמים, against רבי אליעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: It comes to exclude the view of רבי אליעזר, who said the offspring of a שלמים is not brought as a שלמים. He testifies that it is brought.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי פפייס was testifying that the offspring of a שלמים really is offered as a שלמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point of the testimony is not the timing. It is the basic fact that the offspring was brought at all. This argues with רבי אליעזר, who says such offspring cannot be brought as a שלמים.

keyTerms.meaning: To exclude; to reject another opinion
The offspring of an animal set aside as a peace offering
It is offered on the מזבח

steps.whatToRemember: רבי פפייס's testimony teaches that the offspring of a שלמים is brought as a שלמים, against רבי אליעזר. It does not teach that one may delay the offering.

phrases.english: To exclude the view of Rabbi Eliezer,
who said: "The offspring of a peace offering
is not sacrificed as a peace offering,"
he testifies that it is sacrificed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 12 by giving the testimony a new purpose.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the testimony a different purpose
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The testimony seemed to have no point once the delay was explained away.
steps.terutzMaskana: The testimony proves that the offspring of a שלמים is offered as a שלמים, against רבי אליעזר.

steps.title: Offspring and substitute of a thanks offering
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that the offspring and substitutes of a תודה, through all generations, are like a תודה but need no loaves.
steps.simpleTranslation: The offspring of a thanks offering and its substitute, their offspring and the offspring of their offspring, until the end of all generations, are like a thanks offering. The only difference is that they do not need loaves.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches that animals that come from a תודה, or that replace one, are treated as a תודה themselves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A normal תודה is brought with a set of loaves. The משנה says these related animals keep the status of a תודה, but they do not need loaves. This exception is what the גמרא will look for a source for.

keyTerms.meaning: Thanks offering, normally brought with loaves of bread
A substitute animal that someone tried to swap for a קרבן; it becomes holy too
Require the accompanying loaves
The משנה

steps.confusionAlert: They are fully like a תודה in status. The only thing they lack is the loaves. Do not think they stop being a תודה.

phrases.english: Mishnah:
The offspring of a thanks offering and its substitute,
their offspring, and the offspring of their offspring,
until the end of all generations —
these are like a thanks offering,
except that they do not require loaves.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה and a new topic after the שלמים discussion ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The offspring and substitutes of a תודה, through all generations, are treated like a תודה but are not brought with loaves.

steps.title: What is the source?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where the משנה's rule comes from.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: From where are these words derived?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of the משנה's rule. This sets up the ברייתא that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The main question is the source for the exception: why the offspring and substitute of a תודה do not need loaves. The גמרא will answer with a ברייתא that explains a word in the פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: From where are these words (derived)?
The Talmud's discussion of the משנה

phrases.english: Gemara:
From where are these matters derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the משנה in step 14.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source showing that the offspring and substitute of a תודה do not need loaves.

steps.title: A ברייתא on the word 'יקריבנו'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא. It uses the word 'יקריבנו' to teach about a lost תודה that was replaced and then found.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the חכמים taught: What does 'he shall offer it' come to teach? Someone set aside a thanks offering and it was lost. He set aside another one in its place, and then the first one was found, so now both are standing. From where do we know he may offer whichever one he wants, together with its loaves? The פסוק says: 'He shall offer a thanks offering.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its answer by quoting a ברייתא. The ברייתא first uses the פסוק to teach the case of a lost-and-found תודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this case, one animal was lost, a replacement was set aside, and then the first was found. The ברייתא learns from the פסוק that the owner may offer either one, and the one he chooses comes with loaves. This is the first step of the ברייתא. Steps 17-19 finish it and show that offspring and substitutes come without loaves.

keyTerms.meaning: 'He shall offer it'; the word the ברייתא explains
Sets aside an animal as a קרבן
The verse teaches
Its loaves (that come with a תודה)

phrases.english: As the Rabbis taught:
What does "he shall offer it" come to say?
phrases.notes: ויקרא 7:12

phrases.english: One designates a thanks offering, and it was lost,
and he designated another in its place,
and the first was found,
and now both of them are standing.
phrases.notes: Both animals are now available to be brought.

phrases.english: From where do we know that whichever one he wants
he may offer, with its loaves along with it?
The verse states: "He shall offer a thanks offering."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering step 15 by quoting a ברייתא that explains the פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A ברייתא that explains 'יקריבנו'. Its first case: with a lost and replaced תודה, either animal may be offered with its loaves.

steps.title: Only one of the two thank offerings gets loaves
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues. When a lost תודה was replaced and then found, only one of the two animals is brought with loaves.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think the second animal also needs loaves. So the פסוק says 'he shall offer it' (singular): one, and not two.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא keeps going from the last step. It teaches that when there are two thank-offering animals, only one of them comes with loaves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the last step, a תודה was lost, another was set aside in its place, and then the first one was found. One might think each animal needs its own set of loaves. The singular word 'יקריבנו' ('offer it') shows that only one set of loaves is brought, for one animal.

keyTerms.meaning: 'One might think...': opens a wrong first guess that the פסוק then corrects
needs to be brought with loaves (the breads that go with a תודה)
'The פסוק teaches': brings a verse to settle the question
one and not two

phrases.english: One might think the second one also needs loaves?
phrases.notes: The 'second' is the replacement animal set aside after the first תודה was lost.

phrases.english: The verse says: 'he shall offer it'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 7:12

phrases.english: one, and not two.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא quoted in step 16 about the lost and found תודה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The singular 'יקריבנו' limits the loaves to one animal.

steps.title: Offspring, substitutes and replacements are included as a thank offering
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא learns from 'ואם על תודה' that the offspring, substitutes and replacements of a תודה are also brought as a תודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know to include offspring, substitutes and replacements? The פסוק says: 'And if as a thanksgiving.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks how we know that animals connected to a תודה are also offered as a תודה. It answers from a word in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra words 'ואם על תודה' widen the law beyond the original animal. So the offspring, the תמורה, and the replacement for a lost animal are all brought as a תודה. This is the first half of the משנה's rule from step 14.

keyTerms.meaning: to include (to widen a law to more cases)
offspring born to the animal
substitutes: animals someone tried to swap for a holy animal, which become holy too
replacements: animals set aside in place of a lost one

phrases.english: From where do we know to include
offspring, substitutes, and replacements?
The verse says: 'And if as a thanksgiving.'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 7:12

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next piece of the same ברייתא, now covering offspring and substitutes.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'ואם על תודה' includes offspring, substitutes and replacements as a תודה.

steps.title: Only the original thank offering needs loaves
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא learns from 'על זבח התודה' that only the original תודה needs loaves. Its offspring, substitute and replacement do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think all of them need loaves. So the פסוק says 'with the sacrifice of thanksgiving.' The תודה needs loaves, but its offspring, its substitute and its replacement do not need loaves.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes its source. It shows that the extra animals are offered as a תודה but without loaves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 18 put the extra animals into the category of תודה. This step limits one detail: the loaves belong only to 'the' תודה itself. That gives the full source for the משנה in step 14: they are like a תודה but need no loaves.

keyTerms.meaning: the sacrifice of thanksgiving: read as pointing to the original תודה only
its offspring
its substitute
its replacement

steps.whatToRemember: Offspring, substitutes and replacements of a תודה are offered as a תודה, but only the original תודה is brought with loaves.

phrases.english: One might think they all need loaves?
The verse says: 'with the sacrifice of thanksgiving'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 7:12

phrases.english: the thank offering needs loaves,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא וְלָדָהּ וּתְמוּרָתָהּ וַחֲלִיפָתָהּ טְעוּנָה לֶחֶם.
phrases.english: but its offspring, its substitute, and its replacement do not need loaves.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the inclusion from step 18: the extra animals are offered, but without loaves.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The משנה's rule in step 14 is fully sourced: like a תודה, but no loaves.

steps.title: The substitute of a burnt offering and all its offspring are like a burnt offering
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה teaches that the substitute of an עולה, and its offspring for all generations, are treated as an עולה and burned completely.
steps.simpleTranslation: The substitute of an עולה, the offspring of the substitute, and the offspring of its offspring's offspring until the end of time are all like an עולה. They need skinning, cutting into pieces, and being burned completely on the fire.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches that anything that comes from a substitute of an עולה, even many generations later, is treated as a full עולה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The holiness of an עולה passes to its תמורה and on to every later offspring. So all of them get the full עולה treatment: skinning, cutting, and burning the whole animal on the altar.

keyTerms.meaning: burnt offering: burned completely on the altar
skinning the animal
cutting the animal into its parts
burned completely on the altar fire

phrases.english: MISHNA:
The substitute of a burnt offering, the offspring of the substitute,
and the offspring of the offspring of its offspring
until the end of all time
these are like a burnt offering,
and they need skinning and cutting into pieces
and being burned completely in the fire.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the תודה rules, the משנה moves to the same question for an עולה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The substitute of an עולה and all its offspring through every generation are offered as an עולה.

steps.title: A female set aside as a burnt offering that gave birth to a male
steps.stepSummary: The משנה brings a case that is argued about. According to the חכמים, the male calf grazes until it gets a blemish and is sold to buy an עולה. רבי אלעזר says the calf itself is offered.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone set aside a female as an עולה and she gave birth to a male, it grazes until it gets a blemish, is sold, and he brings an עולה with the money. רבי אלעזר says: the calf itself is offered as an עולה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with a case where the חכמים and רבי אלעזר disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עולה must be a male, so the female itself can never be offered. The חכמים say her male calf also cannot be offered directly. Only its money goes to an עולה after it gets a blemish. רבי אלעזר says the male calf is fit, so it goes straight on the altar.

keyTerms.meaning: one who sets aside an animal for a קרבן
a female animal (not fit for an עולה)
it grazes until it gets a blemish that makes it unfit
with its money (the price from selling it)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with step 20. There the mother was a substitute for a real עולה. Here the owner set aside a female directly as an עולה, which can never be offered.

phrases.english: One who sets aside a female as a burnt offering
and she gave birth to a male
it grazes until it becomes unfit,
phrases.notes: He means: until the calf gets a blemish, which lets it be sold.

phrases.english: and it is sold, and he brings a burnt offering with its money.
Rabbi Elazar says:
it itself is offered as a burnt offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second case of the same משנה, this time with an argument.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חכמים: the calf is sold after a blemish and its money buys an עולה. רבי אלעזר: the calf itself is offered.

steps.title: Why is there an argument in the second case but not the first?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the first case of the משנה has no argument while the second case does.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is different about the first case, where they do not argue, and what is different about the second case, where they do argue?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה. The two cases look alike, so why is only one of them argued about?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In both cases the mother cannot go on the altar. A female substitute of an עולה can't be offered, and a female set aside as an עולה can't either. Yet in the first case everyone says the offspring is an עולה, while in the second case the חכמים say it is not. That looks like a contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: what is the difference?
the first clause of the משנה
the last clause of the משנה
they argue

phrases.english: GEMARA:
What is different about the first clause, that they do not argue,
and what is different about the last clause, that they argue?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares the two cases of the משנה just quoted.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's different treatment of its two cases
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both mothers cannot be offered, so the חכמים should argue in the first case too.

steps.title: רבה בר בר חנה: the first case also follows רבי אלעזר
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה answers that the first case is also really argued about, and it follows רבי אלעזר's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said: it is taught as an argument, and it follows רבי אלעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה בר בר חנה answers the question by saying there is no real difference. The first case also follows רבי אלעזר, and the חכמים would disagree there too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He accepts the question's logic: the two cases really are the same. So the first clause of the משנה is not agreed on by everyone. It is רבי אלעזר's view, who lets the offspring be offered.

keyTerms.meaning: it is taught as an argument (there is a dispute about it)

phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Ḥana said:
it is taught as an argument,
phrases.notes: He means the first case of the משנה is also argued about.

phrases.english: and it follows Rabbi Elazar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigns the first clause to one side of the argument
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The first clause seemed to be agreed on by all.
steps.terutzMaskana: The first clause is רבי אלעזר's view alone.

steps.title: רבא: even the חכמים agree in the case of a substitute
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that even the חכמים agree in the first case. With a substitute, the source animal itself goes on the altar, unlike a female set aside as an עולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: you can even say it follows the חכמים. They argue with רבי אלעזר only about someone who sets aside a female as an עולה, whose mother is not offered. But with a substitute, whose mother is also offered, even the חכמים agree.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a different answer. He finds a real difference between the two cases, so the first case can be agreed on by everyone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a female is set aside as an עולה, the holiness starts with an animal that can never be offered. So the חכמים won't offer her calf. With a תמורה, the holiness comes from a real עולה that does go on the altar. So even the חכמים let the offspring be offered.

keyTerms.meaning: you can even say it follows the חכמים
they only argue up to here (their argument is limited to this case)
since its mother is not offered
they agree

steps.whatToRemember: The two answers: רבה בר בר חנה says the first case is רבי אלעזר alone. רבא says everyone agrees there, because the source of a תמורה's holiness is an עולה that is itself offered.
steps.whyThisMatters: רבא shows that the חכמים look at where the holiness came from. If that source animal can be offered, the offspring can be offered too.

phrases.english: And Rava said:
you can even say it follows the Rabbis,

phrases.aramaic: עַד כָּאן לָא פְלִיגִי עֲלֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
phrases.english: they only argue with Rabbi Elazar
about one who sets aside a female as a burnt offering,
since its mother is not offered,
but with a substitute, whose mother is also offered,
phrases.notes: 'Mother' here means the original עולה the substitute got its holiness from, and that animal does go on the altar.

phrases.english: even the Rabbis agree.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to step 22 that disagrees with רבה בר בר חנה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both cases seemed the same, since in each the mother itself cannot be offered.
steps.terutzMaskana: With a תמורה, the holiness comes from an עולה that is offered, so even the חכמים agree that the offspring is offered.

steps.title: Contradiction: רבי אלעזר says to use only the money
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רבי אלעזר really holds that the offspring itself is offered. In another משנה about the substitute of an אשם, he only says to bring an עולה with the money from selling it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did רבי אלעזר really say the animal itself is offered as an עולה? But look at this משנה: the substitute of an אשם, the offspring of that substitute, their offspring and their offspring's offspring forever, all graze until they get a blemish. Then they are sold, and the money goes to gift offerings. רבי אליעזר says: they are left to die. רבי אלעזר says: bring an עולה with their money. So with the money, yes; with the animal itself, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי אלעזר's ruling from step 21. It quotes a different משנה where רבי אלעזר seems to say the animal itself may NOT be offered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 21, רבי אלעזר said the offspring itself is brought as an עולה. Here, about animals that come from an אשם, he only allows using their sale money to buy an עולה. That suggests he does not let such an animal itself be offered, which looks like a contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: And raise a contradiction against it (from another source)
An animal swapped in for an אשם (guilt offering)
They graze until they get a blemish
A gift offering, a voluntary sacrifice
With the money (from selling the animal)

steps.confusionAlert: Two names look almost the same here. רבי אליעזר (with a yud) says the animals are left to die. רבי אלעזר (without a yud) is the one the whole question is about.

phrases.english: And did Rabbi Elazar really say
that the animal itself is offered as a burnt offering?
phrases.notes: This points back to רבי אלעזר's view in the earlier משנה about the calf of a female set aside as an עולה.

phrases.english: But raise a contradiction:
The substitute of a guilt offering, the offspring of that substitute,
their offspring, and the offspring of their offspring
until the end of all time —
they graze until they get a blemish,
and they are sold, and their money goes to gift offerings.
Rabbi Eliezer says: they are left to die.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר: יָבִיא בִּדְמֵיהֶן עוֹלָה.
phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar says: he should bring a burnt offering with their money.
With the money — yes,
the animal itself — no.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר יִקְרַב עוֹלָה הוּא עַצְמוֹ? וּרְמִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the question about the משנה's structure (steps 22-24) to a contradiction within רבי אלעזר's own rulings.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's ruling in step 21 that the offspring itself is offered as an עולה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the case of a substitute of an אשם, רבי אלעזר only says to use the money for an עולה. This implies the animal itself cannot be offered, which contradicts his ruling in step 21.

steps.title: רב חסדא: רבי אלעזר was arguing within the חכמים' view
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא answers that רבי אלעזר really holds the animal itself is offered. He only mentioned the money because he was arguing with the חכמים on their own terms.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: רבי אלעזר was speaking to the חכמים according to their own view. He told them: I myself hold that even the offspring itself is offered as an עולה. But you say it grazes until it gets a blemish. At least admit that the leftover money goes to an individual's gift offerings. And they answered him: the leftover money goes to communal gift offerings.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא resolves the contradiction. He says רבי אלעזר's ruling about the money was not his own true opinion. It was a point he made inside the חכמים' approach.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Personally, רבי אלעזר holds that the animal itself is offered, just like in step 21. In this משנה he was only arguing about where the money goes if we follow the חכמים: an individual's offering or a communal one. So his mention of the money says nothing against his own view.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the words (view) of the חכמים
According to me, I hold
At least admit to me
Leftovers, here the money from selling these animals
A gift offering of an individual / a gift offering of the community

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a common move in the גמרא. A sage's statement may be an argument within his opponents' view, not his own final opinion.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר לְדִבְרֵיהֶם דְּרַבָּנַן קָאָמַר לְהוּ,
phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar was speaking to them according to the Rabbis' own view,
saying: According to me, I hold
that even the offspring itself is also offered as a burnt offering,
but according to you, who say it grazes —
at least admit to me
that the leftover money goes to an individual's gift offerings,
And they said to him:
the leftover money goes to communal gift offerings.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר לְדִבְרֵיהֶם דְּרַבָּנַן קָאָמַר לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 25.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Recasting the statement as an argument within the opponents' view (לדבריהם).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since רבי אלעזר mentioned only the money, we thought he holds the animal itself cannot be offered.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי אלעזר personally holds that even the offspring itself is offered. His statement about the money only argues about who the money goes to, within the חכמים' approach.

steps.title: רבא: The cases differ, because the mother is called עולה
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives a different answer. רבי אלעזר only lets the animal itself be offered when a female was set aside as an עולה, because then the mother carries the name עולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: רבי אלעזר only said that the animal itself is offered as an עולה in the case of someone who sets aside a female as an עולה, since the mother has the name עולה on it...
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the contradiction a different way, by showing that the two cases are not the same. His explanation continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 21, the mother was set aside as an עולה, so the name עולה is already on the mother. That is why רבי אלעזר lets the offspring itself go on the altar. In the case of the אשם, there is no such עולה name on the source animal, so only the money can buy an עולה.

keyTerms.meaning: He only said this (in this specific case), not in other cases
One who sets aside a female animal as an עולה
The name or status of an עולה

phrases.english: Rava said:

phrases.aramaic: עַד כַּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar only said
that the animal itself is offered as a burnt offering
in the case of one who sets aside a female as a burnt offering,
since there is the name of a burnt offering on its mother,

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: עַד כַּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר הוּא עַצְמוֹ יִקְרַב עוֹלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second answer to the contradiction in step 25, different from רב חסדא's answer in step 26.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both cases are alike, so רבי אלעזר contradicts himself.
steps.terutzMaskana: In the case of a female set aside as an עולה, the mother carries the name עולה, so the offspring itself may be offered. The אשם case lacks this.
